  CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE

MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the City Council
  January 26, 2022

CALL TO ORDER:

This regular meeting of the Westlake Village City Council was called to order by Mayor
Halpern on Wednesday, January 26, 2022, at 6:38 p.m., at 31200 Oak Crest Drive,
Westlake Village via teleconference due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and
pursuant to Government Code Section 54953(e).

Mayor Halpern called for a moment of silence to honor Los Angeles County Fire fighter
Johnathan Flagler.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

Mayor Halpern led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:

PRESENT:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Mayor Halpern
ABSENT:  None

Also Present:  City Manager de Geus, City Attorney Boga, Deputy City Manager
  Eskandar, Administrative Services Director Wilson, Planning
  Director Forbes, City Clerk Mann, City Engineer Hughes, Associate
  Planner Sinkula and Deputy City Clerk Kramer

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

Councilmember Mcsweeney moved to  approve  the  Agenda  as  presented .
Councilmember Davis seconded the motion.

  YES:  Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, Councilmember Davis,
  Councilmember Honig, Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0

  Councilmember Mcsweeney seconded the motion.  -
  ===;

  Councilmember Honig, Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO:  None

  ABSTAIN :  None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0.

  SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS: None

  PUBLIC COMMENTS: None.

  COUNCIL RESPONSE: None

  STAFF COMMENTS:

  City Manager de Geus reported that the pedestrian hybrid beacon on Triunfo Canyon
  Road at Saddle Mountain Drive was activated on January 25, 2022; related to COVID-19
  City Hall remains closed due to Omicron variant and plans to reopen on January 31, 2022.
  City Manager de Geus expressed appreciation to Deputy City Clerk Kramer for her
  assistance with the City Clerk duties and presented Deputy City Clerk Kramer with
  flowers.

  COUNCIL COMMENTS:

  Councilmembers commented on the increased importance of the Las Virgenes/Malibu
  Council of Governments (LVMCOG) and thanked Councilmember Honig for her
  leadership as the Past President of LVMCOG.

  Mayor Halpern reminded residents to shop local and welcomed City Clerk Mann.

  MONTHLY DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

  1.  Sheriffs Department Report
  Deputy Brian Knott presented the Sheriff Department's crime and traffic report for
  the month of October, November, and December 2021 and commented on testing
  the new pedestrian hybrid beacon on January 26, 2022 and issued 27 citations.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  January 26, 2022  3

MONTHLY DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS (continued):

  Lieutenant Watters responded to City Council questions regarding recent crimes,
  street racing, and sight line signage.

2.  Fire Department Report
  Community Services Liaison Megan Currier presented the Fire Department's
  report for the months of October, November, and December 2021, reflecting the
  fire prevention, medical services, and rescue activities conducted. Reported that
  due to COVID, Fire Department facilities are closed and in-person events are on
  hold until further notice.

3.  Chamber of Commerce Report
  Adam Haverstock, Director of Government Affairs and Tourism, welcomed City
  Clerk Mann and highlighted recent and upcoming events of the Greater Conejo
  Valley Chamber of Commerce which will be held virtually. Encouraged businesses
  to visit their website to sign up for COVID supplies and Human Resource materials.

4.  Library Report
  Julie Frieze, Manager of the Westlake Village Daniel K. Ludwig Library presented
  the report for the months of October, November, and December 2021 covering
  traffic, circulation, and reference requests. Ms. Frieze commented that due to the
  Omicron variant, in-person programs are on hold and in the month of January,
  capacity is reduced to 50%.

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

1.  TELECOMMUNICATIONS/CONNECTIVITY/IT COMMITTEE REPORT

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item, which was an update on the
  Telecommunications/Connectivity/IT Committee meeting held on July 23, 2021,
  regarding the design revisions to the City's website.

  Deputy City Manager Eskandar presented staff's report providing an overview of
  the design revisions to the City's website which consisted of a proposed layout,
  photographs, color palette, and global navigation functions. He noted that the
  redesign is included in the current contract with CivicPlus with no additional cost.
  Mr. Eskandar stated that the City's goal was to deliver a modern website that offers
  usability, accessibility, functionality, and customer service to the community and
  that following the City Council's review, CivicPlus will need approximately six to
  eight weeks for the new website to be configured and launched.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  January 26. 2022  4

PUBLIC HEARINGS:

1.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR  CONDITIONAL  USE  PERMIT  NO.  21-009:
  RESOLUTION NO. 2231-22

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and Associate Planner Sinkula
  presented the request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 21-009
  to authorize the sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits for onsite consumption and
  the use of a 1,250 square foot outdoor dining area as part of the operation of the
  restaurant located at 32123 Lindero Canyon Road, Suite 109, within The Landing
  Center. Hamid Sadraie filed the request on behalf of The Landing Grill & Sushi
  Bar.

  Associate Planner Sinkula reported that through the City's COVID-19 Temporary
  Outdoor Dining Area program that was enacted by the City Council in 2020, The
  Landing temporarily expanded their footprint/service area beyond the covered
  outdoor dining area. Since the service of alcohol in the temporary outdoor area is
  tied to the alcohol license, the restaurant would be able to continue serving beer,
  wine and distilled spirits in the temporary outdoor area if the CUP request is
  approved by the City Council. Mrs. Sinkula noted that this could continue so long
  as the City's Temporary Outdoor Dining Area program is in effect, its
  terms/conditions are complied with, and the California Department of Alcoholic
  Beverage Control allows.

  On January 5, 2022, the Land Use Committee (Pearl/Honig) reviewed the CUP
  request and recommended that the request move forward to a public hearing.

  City Councilmembers complimented Mr. Sadraie as a business owner and
  community partner.

  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved to approve Resolution No. 2231-22, "A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Westlake Village approving Conditional
  Use Permit No. 21-009 to authorize the sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits for
  on site consumption and the use of a 1,250 sq. ft. outdoor dining area as part of the
  operation of The Landing Grill and Sushi Bar located at 32123 Lindero Canyon
  Road, Suite 109" be adopted. Councilmember Davis seconded the motion.

  YES:  Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, Councilmember Davis,
  Councilmember Honig, Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0 .
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  January 26 , 2022  5

PUBLIC HEARINGS (continued):

2.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR REALLOCATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2021-22 AND
  ALLOCATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM FUNDS AND CARES ACT FUNDS: RESOLUTION
  NO. 2232-22

  Planning Director Forbes presented staff's report outlining the Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) program. Since 1981 the City has received
  funding from the CDBG program through the Los Angeles County Development
  Authority (LACDA), the average annual allocation has been approximately
  $26,000; last year's allocation was $30,712, and that the program provides grants
  up to $5,000 to low- and moderate-income Westlake Village homeowners to make
  certain home improvements and needed repairs. The program has not consistently
  fully expended the available funds leading to an unallocated fund balance of
  $76,023 for FY 2021-22. In addition to CDBG funds, the City was allocated
  $18,250 in CDBG-CV funds from the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic
  Security (CARES) Act which must be spent on efforts related to recovery from the
  coronavirus pandemic, including assistance programs for affected businesses.

  Staff's recommendation is to allocate the City's full annual CDBG allocation of
  $30,533 to the Housing Rehabilitation Program as in prior years and allocate all
  funding that was earmarked for business grant and rental assistance programs last
  year plus all remaining unallocated funds to LACDA's Small Business Grant
  Program launching in February 2022. This total funding of $99,980 includes
  $81,730 in CDBG funds and $18,250 in CDBG-CV funds. Funds provided by
  Westlake Village to the LACDA program would be used only for Westlake Village
  businesses. This amount could fund $10,000 grants for up to nine businesses, with
  the balance covering administration costs.

  Councilmember Davis moved that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2232-22
  titled 'A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Westlake Village Approving
  Reallocations for Fiscal Year 2021-22 and Allocations for Fiscal Year 2022-23" for
  Community Development Block Grant Programs. Mayor Pro Tern Pearl seconded
  the motion.

  YES:  Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, Councilmember Davis,
  Councilmember Honig, Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN :  None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  January 26. 2022  6

  MONTHLY IN-HOUSE DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

  1.  Engineering Department Report
  City Engineer Hughes highlighted various items from the Engineering
  Status Report which included the pedestrian hybrid beacon activation
  (Triunfo Canyon Road at Saddle Mountain Drive), concept design beginning
  on the pickleball courts at Community Park, traffic signal pole painting
  project status, working on the asset management plan with Kayuga
  Solutions, and Watershed Area Steering Committee (WASC) presentation
  received by staff.

  2.  Planning Department Report
  Planning Director Forbes reviewed the Planning Department's Status
  Report which included a Senate Bill (SB) 9 Development Standards
  handout posted on website. Future Land Use Committee topics will include
  updated Oak Tree and Heritage Tree Preservation Standards for review,
  and the Westlake Village Municipal Code to ensure it reflects current legal
  requirements to re-adopt the Los Angeles County Code.

  3.  Cultural Recreation Report
  City Manager de Geus highlighted various items from the Cultural
  Recreation Department's Status Report which included that Conejo Parks
  and Recreation activities are being held virtually or outdoors, community
  meeting rooms at City Hall will remain closed through February, plans are
  underway to bring back a July 4th Fireworks show.

  City Manager de Geus discussed the challenges in Cultural Recreation due
  to staffing departures and capacity issues; announced that the February
  Westlake Discovers will be postponed.

  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved to approve the Consent Calendar. Councilmember
  Davis seconded the motion.

  YES:  Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, Councilmember Davis,
  Councilmember Honig, Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN :  None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0.
